title: sqlops Module
content_markdown: SQLops (SQL-operations) modules implements a set of script functions for generic SQL standard queries (raw or structure queries). It also provides a dedicated set of functions for DB manipulation (loading/storing/removing) of user AVPs (preferences).
overview: SQLops (SQL-operations) modules implements a set of script functions for generic SQL standard queries (raw or structure queries). It also provides a dedicated set of functions for DB manipulation (loading/storing/removing) of user AVPs (preferences).

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: DB URL for database connection. As the module allows the usage of multiple DBs (DB URLs), the actual DB URL may be preceded by an reference number. This reference number is to be passed to AVPOPS function that what to explicitly use this DB connection. If no reference number is given, 0 is assumed - this is the default DB URL.
exported_parameters.example_code:
# default URL
modparam("sqlops","db\_url","mysql://user:passwd@host/database")
# an additional DB URL
modparam("sqlops","db\_url","1 postgres://user:passwd@host2/opensips")
exported_parameters.notes: This parameter is optional, it's default value being NULL.

exported_parameters.name: usr_table
exported_parameters.description: DB table to be used for user preferences (AVPs)
exported_parameters.notes: This parameter is optional, it's default value being “usr\_preferences”.

exported_parameters.name: db_scheme
exported_parameters.description: Definition of a DB scheme to be used for accessing a non-standard User Preference -like table. Definition of a DB scheme. Scheme syntax is: *db\_scheme = name':'element\[';'element\]\* *element* = 'uuid\_col='string | 'username\_col='string | 'domain\_col='string | 'value\_col='string | 'value\_type='('integer'|'string') | 'table='string

exported_parameters.name: use_domain
exported_parameters.description: If the domain part of the a SIP URI should be used for identifying an AVP in DB operations.

exported_parameters.name: ps_id_max_buf_len
exported_parameters.description: The maximum size of the buffer used to build the query IDs which are used for managing the Prepare Statements when comes to the "sql\_select|update|insert|replace|delete()" functions. If the size is exceeded (when trying to build the PS query ID), the PS support will be dropped for the query. If set to 0, the PS support will be completly disabled.

exported_parameters.name: bigint_to_str
exported_parameters.description: Controls bigint conversion. By default bigint values are returned as int. If the value stored in bigint is out of the int range, by enabling bigint to string conversion, the bigint value will be returned as string.

exported_parameters.name: uuid_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of column containing the uuid (unique user id).

exported_parameters.name: username_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of column containing the username.

exported_parameters.name: domain_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of column containing the domain name.

exported_parameters.name: attribute_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of column containing the attribute name (AVP name).

exported_parameters.name: value_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of column containing the AVP value.

exported_parameters.name: type_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of column containing the AVP type.

exported_functions.name: sql_query

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: must be a valid SQL query. The parameter can contain pseudo-variables. You must escape any pseudo-variables manually to prevent SQL injection attacks.

parameters.name: res_col_avps
parameters.description: a list with AVP names where to store the result. The format is "$avp(name1);$avp(name2);...". If the result consists of multiple rows, then multiple AVPs with corresponding names will be added. The value type of the AVP (string or integer) will be derived from the type of the columns. If the value in the database is NULL, the returned avp will be a string with the <null> value.

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the "db_url" module parameter. It can be either a constant, or a string/int variable.

return_values.condition: the query returned an empty result set

exported_functions.description: Make a database query and store the result in AVPs.

exported_functions.name: sql_query_one

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: must be a valid SQL query. The parameter can contain pseudo-variables.

parameters.name: res_col_vars
parameters.description: variables for returning the query result may any kind of variable, of course, as time as it is writeable. NOTE that the number of return vairable MUST match (as number) the number of returned columns. If less variables are provided, the query will fail.

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the "db_url" module parameter. It can be either a constant, or a string/int variable.

exported_functions.description: Similar to sql_query(), it makes a generic raw database query and returns the results, but with the following differences: returns only one row - even if the query results in a multi row result, only the first row will be returned to script. return variables are not limited to AVPs - the variables for returning the query result may any kind of variable, of course, as time as it is writeable. NOTE that the number of return vairable MUST match (as number) the number of returned columns. If less variables are provided, the query will fail. NULL is returned - any a DB NULL value resulting from the query will be pushed as NULL indicator (and NOT as <null> string) to the script variables.

examples.code:
sql_query_one("SELECT password, ha1 FROM subscriber WHERE username='$tU'",
	"$var(pass);$var(hash)");
# $var(pass) or $var(hash) may be NULL if the corresponding columns
# are not populated
...
sql_query_one("SELECT value, type FROM usr_preferences WHERE username='$fU' and attribute='cfna'",
	"$var(cf_uri);$var(type)");
# the above query will return only one row, even if there are multiple `cfna`
# attributes for the user

exported_functions.name: sql_select

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: JSON formated string holding an array of columns to be returned by the select. Ex: "["col1","col2"]". If missing, a "*" (all columns) select will be performed.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: the name of the table to be queried.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: JSON formated string holding the "where" filter of the query. This must be an array of (column, operator,value) pairs. The exact JSON syntax of such a pair is "{"column":{"operator":"value"}}".; operators may be `>`, `<`, `=`, `!=` or custom string; The values may be string, integer or `null`. To simplify the usage with the `=` operator, you can use "{"column":"value"}" If missing, all rows will be selected.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: the name of the column to oder by (only ascending).

parameters.name: res_col_avps
parameters.description: a list with AVP names where to store the result. The format is "$avp(name1);$avp(name2);...". If this parameter is omitted, the result is stored in "$avp(1);$avp(2);...". If the result consists of multiple rows, then multiple AVPs with corresponding names will be added. The value type of the AVP (string or integer) will be derived from the type of the columns. If the value in the database is NULL, the returned avp will be a string with the <null> value.

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the db_url module parameter. It can be either a constant, or a string/int variable.

return_values.condition: the query returned an empty result set

exported_functions.description: Function to perform a structured (not raw) SQL SELECT operation. The query is performed via OpenSIPS internal SQL interface, taking advantages of the prepared-statements support (if the db backend provides something like that). The selected columns are returned into a set of AVPs (one to one matching the selected columns).

exported_functions.name: sql_select_one

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: JSON formated string holding an array of columns to be returned by the select.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: the name of the table to be queried.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: JSON formated string holding the "where" filter of the query. This must be an array of (column, operator,value) pairs.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: the name of the column to oder by (only ascending).

parameters.name: res_col_vars
parameters.description: variables for returning the query result may any kind of variable, of course, as time as it is writeable. NOTE that the number of return vairable MUST match (as number) the number of returned columns. If less variables are provided, the query will fail.

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the db_url module parameter. It can be either a constant, or a string/int variable.

exported_functions.description: Similar to sql_select(), it makes a SELECT SQL query and returns the results, but with the following differences: returns only one row - even if the query results in a multi row result, only the first row will be returned to script. return variables are not limited to AVPs - the variables for returning the query result may any kind of variable, of course, as time as it is writeable. NOTE that the number of return vairable MUST match (as number) the number of returned columns. If less variables are provided, the query will fail. NULL is returned - any a DB NULL value resulting from the query will be pushed as NULL indicator (and NOT as <null> string) to the script variables.

examples.code:
sql_select_one('["value","type"]', 'usr_preferences',
	'[ {"username": "$tu"}, {"attribute": "cfna"}]', ,
	'$var(cf_uri);$var(type)');
# the above query will return only one row, even if there are multiple `cfna`
# attributes for the user

exported_functions.name: sql_update

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: JSON formated string holding an array of (column,value) pairs to be updated by the query. Ex: "[{"col1":"val1"},{"col2":"val1"}]".

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: the name of the table to be queried.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: JSON formated string holding the "where" filter of the query. This must be an array of (column, operator,value) pairs. The exact JSON syntax of such a pair is "{"column":{"operator":"value"}}".; operators may be `>`, `<`, `=`, `!=` or custom string; The values may be string, integer or `null`. To simplify the usage with the `=` operator, you can use "{"column":"value"}" If missing, all rows will be updated.

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the db_url module parameter. It can be either a constant, or a string/int variable.

exported_functions.description: Function to perform a structured (not raw) SQL UPDATE operation. IMPORTANT: please see all the general notes from the sql_select() function.

parameters.name: columns

parameters.name: db_id

exported_functions.name: sql_replace

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: the name of the table to be queried.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: JSON formated string holding an array of (column,value) pairs to be replaced.

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id).

exported_functions.description:
Function very similar to sql_insert() function, but performing an SQL REPLACE operation instead. Note that not all SQL backend in OpenSIPS may support a REPLACE operation.

The function returns true if the query was successful.

exported_functions.name: sql_avp_load

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: what info is used for identifying the AVPs. Parameter syntax: source = (pvar|str_value) ['/'('username'|'domain'|'uri'|'uuid')]). pvar = any pseudo variable defined in OpenSIPS. If the pvar is $ru (request uri), $fu (from uri), $tu (to uri) or $ou (original uri), then the implicit flag is 'uri'. Otherwise, the implicit flag is 'uuid'.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: which AVPs will be loaded from DB into memory. Parameter syntax is: name = avp_spec['/'(table_name|'$'db_scheme)]

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the "db_url" module parameter.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: static string which will precede the names of the AVPs populated by this function.

return_values.condition: if it loaded some values in AVPs

exported_functions.description:
Loads from DB into memory the AVPs corresponding to the given source. If given, it sets the script flags for loaded AVPs. It returns true if it loaded some values in AVPs, false otherwise (db error, no avp loaded ...).

AVPs may be preceded by an optional prefix, in order to avoid some conflicts.

exported_functions.name: sql_avp_store

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: what info is used for identifying the AVPs. Parameter syntax: source = (pvar|str_value) ['/'('username'|'domain'|'uri'|'uuid')]). pvar = any pseudo variable defined in OpenSIPS. If the pvar is $ru (request uri), $fu (from uri), $tu (to uri) or $ou (original uri), then the implicit flag is 'uri'. Otherwise, the implicit flag is 'uuid'.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: which AVPs will be stored to DB. Parameter syntax is: name = avp_spec['/'(table_name|'$'db_scheme)]

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the "db_url" module parameter.

exported_functions.description:
Stores to DB the AVPs corresponding to the given source.

The meaning and usage of the parameters are identical as for sql_avp_load(source, name) function. Please refer to its description.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: what info is used for identifying the AVPs. Parameter syntax: source = (pvar|str_value) ['/'('username'|'domain'|'uri'|'uuid')]) pvar = any pseudo variable defined in OpenSIPS. If the pvar is $ru (request uri), $fu (from uri), $tu (to uri) or $ou (original uri), then the implicit flag is 'uri'. Otherwise, the implicit flag is 'uuid'.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: which AVPs will be loaded from DB into memory. Parameter syntax is: name = avp_spec['/'(table_name|'$'db_scheme)]

parameters.name: db_id
parameters.description: reference to a defined DB URL (a numerical id) - see the “db_url” module parameter.

exported_functions.description: Deletes from DB the AVPs corresponding to the given _source_. The meaning and usage of the parameters are identical as for _sql_avp_load(source, name)_ function. Please refer to its description.
